intervals.label: HERA I at 820 GeV protons (first data in summer 1992)
intervals.note: Year precision. The proton energy was raised from 820 to 920 GeV in 1998 (the quote of the proton-energy value); the electron beam was about 27.5 GeV throughout.
intervals.quote: The first HERA data were taken in summer 1992.

cms_energy.quote: The data were taken with the H1 detector at the HERA storage ring in 1994, in which 27.5 GeV positrons collided with 820 GeV protons at a centre of mass energy sqrt{s}=300 GeV.

proton_energy.quote: The energy of the proton beam was initially set to 820 GeV until it was increased to 920 GeV, in 1998, and kept at that value.

intervals.label: operation
intervals.locator: DESY brochure 'HERA - Pointing the way' (2007), PDF p. 4 (start 1992, research operation concluded end of June 2007); end day: Zhang for H1 and ZEUS, arXiv:0812.4662, introduction
intervals.note: DESY's brochure gives the start (1992) and says research operation concluded at the end of June 2007; the day comes from arXiv:0812.4662 (for the H1 and ZEUS Collaborations): "The electron-proton collider HERA ended its data taking on June 30, 2007." Operating interval; the terminal event is its end.
intervals.quote: The Hadron-Electron Ring Accelerator HERA went into operation at DESY in 1992. Research operation was concluded at the end of June 2007 and the accelerator was switched off.

intervals.label: HERA at 920 GeV protons (from 1998)
intervals.locator: Klein and Yoshida, section 1 (arXiv:0805.3334); abstract of arXiv:hep-ex/0106022
intervals.note: Year precision for the start ("in 1998"); the end is the end of HERA operation. HERA II (2003 to 2007) kept 27.5 GeV electrons and 920 GeV protons ("with electron (positron) energy of approximately 27.5 GeV and proton energy of 920 GeV"). In the last three months of operation (2007) data with lowered proton energies of 460 and 575 GeV were taken ("In the last three months of HERA operation, data with lowered proton beam energies of 460 GeV and 575 GeV were taken"); the centre-of-mass energies of those runs are not stated in the sources read, so they are not recorded as eras.
intervals.quote: The energy of the proton beam was initially set to 820 GeV until it was increased to 920 GeV, in 1998, and kept at that value.

cms_energy.locator: abstract of arXiv:hep-ex/0106022; Klein and Yoshida (about 320 GeV)
cms_energy.note: The upper end of the 300-318 GeV range the abstract gives for the HERA runs, equal to 2*sqrt(27.5 GeV * 920 GeV) = 318 GeV from the beam energies; Klein and Yoshida write "about 320 GeV" (the record's headline).
cms_energy.quote: At HERA, new physics processes beyond the SM are probed in e^+/- proton collisions at a center of mass energy of 300-318 GeV.

proton_energy.note: Proton energy from 1998 until the end of operation.
proton_energy.quote: The energy of the proton beam was initially set to 820 GeV until it was increased to 920 GeV, in 1998, and kept at that value.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.locator: Zhang for H1 and ZEUS, arXiv:0812.4662, introduction
intervals.note: Terminal event: the end of the operating interval above. The paper says data taking ended on that day; DESY's brochure says research operation was concluded at the end of June 2007 and the accelerator switched off.
intervals.quote: The electron-proton collider HERA ended its data taking on June 30, 2007.

name: Hadron-Elektron-Ring-Anlage
notes: Injector chain (Klein & Yoshida 2008, Table 1): protons, RFQ - LINAC III (50 MeV) - DESY III (8 GeV) - PETRA (40 GeV) - HERA (920 GeV); electrons and positrons, LINAC II (450 MeV) - PIA - DESY II (7 GeV) - PETRA (12 GeV) - HERA (27.5 GeV). Only HERA has an Atlas record; the pre-accelerators and PETRA are not linked.

Operation dates: DESY's page says "Research operation: 1992-2007" and Klein & Yoshida say "The first HERA data were taken in summer 1992. It ceased operations in June 2007"; the day (30 June 2007) is from Zhang for H1 and ZEUS (arXiv:0812.4662): "The electron-proton collider HERA ended its data taking on June 30, 2007." It stays on the interval with its low confidence.

Eras (2026-10-26, follow-ups 2): the cms energy was 300 GeV with 820 GeV protons (1992 to 1998) and 318 GeV with 920 GeV protons (1998 to 2007); the headline 320 GeV is Klein and Yoshida's rounded figure for the second era.

beam_energy.note: Replaces the earlier lecture-notes sourcing. Table 1 of the same paper gives the lepton ring energy as 27.5 GeV.
beam_energy.quote: The energy of the electron (positron) beam was about 27.5 GeV.

circumference.note: DESY's own figure (the same page says "a 6.3-kilometer-long tunnel"). Klein & Yoshida (arXiv:0805.3334), Table 1 caption, write "The main ring is 6223 m in circumference", which differs by 1.8 %; the DESY figure is used and agrees with the tunnel geometry check on the DESY map.

cms_energy.quote: From 1992 to 2007, HERA, the first electron-proton collider, operated at cms energies of about 320 GeV

injection_energy.display: 40 GeV (protons from PETRA); 12 GeV (electrons from PETRA)
injection_energy.note: Table 1, "Chain of (pre)accelerators at HERA and their energies": protons source, RFQ (750 keV), LINAC III (50 MeV), DESY III (8 GeV), PETRA (40 GeV), HERA (920 GeV); electrons source (150 keV), LINAC II (450 MeV), PIA (450 MeV), DESY II (7 GeV), PETRA (12 GeV), HERA (27.5 GeV). PETRA belongs to the colliders stream and has no record on this branch.

proton_energy.note: 820 GeV until 1998, 920 GeV from 1998; in the last three months of operation lower proton energies (460 and 575 GeV) were used (same paper).
proton_energy.quote: The energy of the proton beam was initially set to 820 GeV until it was increased to 920 GeV, in 1998, and kept at that value.

summary.plain: HERA was DESY's electron-proton collider in Hamburg, Germany, the only collider in the world that brought electrons or positrons into collision with protons. It ran in a 6.3-kilometre tunnel from 1992 to 2007, and its experiments used the collisions to study the inner structure of the proton.
summary.technical: Electron/positron-proton storage-ring collider at DESY, 6336 m long (DESY figure): 27.5 GeV electrons or positrons on 820 GeV protons (cms 300 GeV) from 1992, then on 920 GeV protons (cms about 320 GeV) from 1998. The collider detectors H1 and ZEUS ran from 1992; HERMES (lepton beam) and HERA-B (proton beam) were fixed-target experiments. Research operation ended on 30 June 2007.
